title: AI-Generated Hot Girls Are Ripping Off Comedians to Boost Their Horny Content
gist: AI-generated 'hot girl' Instagram accounts are lifting stand-up comedians' jokes verbatim and funneling audiences to Fanvue/OnlyFans-style content, while Meta declines to treat it as a policy violation and copyright offers comics little recourse.

insights.claim: AI-generated influencer Aylen Skye (250,000 Instagram followers) posted a verbatim copy of comedian Julia Jasunas' joke and links to a Fanvue page, a subscription platform marketing itself as the 'No1 AI monetisation platform for creators'.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Shows AI accounts monetizing stolen viral content via adult subscription platforms.
insights.locator: The video was of a purported stand-up comic

insights.claim: WIRED identified eight comics whose viral clips were replicated by scantily clad AI-generated women, with better lighting, sound and outfits, often reaching bigger audiences than the originals.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Algorithmic engagement favors polished AI clones, a risk for human creator economics.

insights.claim: Generation quality for clone videos improved exponentially from June to October; an account called Tiffany Sloane built 375,000+ Instagram followers since August and spread to TikTok and Facebook as a 'super horny AI-generated short-form video content farm'.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Fast improvement in AI video realism lowers the cost of scaled content farms.

insights.claim: Comedian George Brett Olson's joke was cloned by Sloane in near-identical staging; Sloane commented 'sorry, won't happen again' and deleted its video and many other Reels after his viral callout.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Public shaming works on individual accounts but not at platform scale.

insights.claim: Instagram's guidelines prohibit impersonation but not copying non-copyrighted content, and allow AI content if labeled; Meta told creators the AI clones did not violate community guidelines, and all accounts flagged by WIRED remain on the platform.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Platform policy leaves AI content farms unconstrained, a reputational and trust risk for Meta.
insights.locator: Though Instagram’s community guidelines prohibit impersonation

insights.claim: Instagram head Adam Mosseri said it is not practical to ban AI content but that Meta is invested in driving traffic to original creators and should work out what to do about wholesale rip-offs.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Signals Meta will tune ranking rather than ban; watch for original-content distribution changes.
insights.locator: After tagging Instagram head Adam Mosseri

insights.claim: Jokes enjoy little copyright protection and low dollar stakes deter litigation; an IP lawyer reportedly told Olson that unless Sloane earned millions on OnlyFans a lawsuit was probably not worth it.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Weak IP protection plus low damages makes small-creator content cheap to exploit.
insights.locator: As of now, there’s very little that comedians can do

insights.claim: Andreessen Horowitz partner Justine Moore publicly praised Sloane as 'a genius marketing hack', illustrating that parts of the tech industry do not share creators' negative view of AI-generated influencers.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: VC enthusiasm for AI influencers signals capital flowing toward the model despite creator backlash.
insights.locator: The negative sentiment against these AI-generated creators

insights.claim: Olson argues the follower counts of AI accounts show audiences do not care whether the artist is real, calling this demoralizing.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Audience indifference to authenticity is the demand-side driver of AI content farms.
insights.quote: To me, we're asking the essential question, does the artist matter?
